text:
Kent Johnson finally has the role the fifth overall pick in 2021 was supposed to get. He plays 18:27 a night, up from 13:14 last season, and he's on the ice for 84% of Columbus's power-play chances, up from 37%. The result: 22 points in 22 games after 22 points in 76 last season. Our numbers call it a breakout, and he ranks 17th in the league in wins added by goals.

The role change is real, and so is a step up in his own chances, 0.95 expected goals per 60 from 0.69. The finishing is the part to treat carefully: nine goals on 6.4 expected, shooting 18% after 6% last season. His point rate (3.25 per 60) is far above his talent range, so some cooling is coming. All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) says his offense lives in transition, 52% of his shots off the rush. Our range projects 51 to 74 points. Even the low end would be a career year.
